text:
anna: ran an overnight microburst stress for the new q8 quant Llama2-70b bringup. compared flashattn-v2, flashattn-v3, triton vendor kernels across H100/A100 in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. seeing weird p99 spikes with flashv3 on H100 when traffic is bursty (1-5 req/s bursts). summary below. :thinking:

anna: quick summary (seq=4096, batch=1, 95th/99th in ms)
- H100 flashv3: median 22ms, p95 48ms, p99 210ms (spiky during microbursts)
- H100 flashv2: median 24ms, p95 55ms, p99 92ms
- A100 triton: median 40ms, p95 85ms, p99 125ms
- H100 vendor-lib: median 25ms, p95 60ms, p99 110ms

raj: can you paste the bench command you used?

anna: sure, ran the harness with the same load pattern: 
```
python infra/bench/run_perf.py --model llama2-70b-q8 --kernel flashattn-v3 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --pattern microburst --bursts 100 --burst_qps 5 --idle 15
```

kevin: interesting. two immediate suspects: kernel warmup/compile and kv-cache concurrency. flashv3 changed the kernel selection heuristics and we saw compile-on-first-path for some kernel shapes. did you see any "compiling kernel" logs?

anna: yes, noticed these at the start of many bursts: "[info] compiling fused_attn kernel shape=(b=1, seq=4096, heads=64)" — compile latency ~150ms in some cases. those compile spikes line up with p99s. also saw occasional "kv-cache stall" warnings when many short-lived requests hit same worker.

sarah: we ran into similar pattern on a customer workload last quarter. flashv3 gave lower median but introduces on-demand codegen for rare shapes which causes tail spikes. we mitigated with two things: prewarming common kernel shapes at boot, and switching kernel-selection hysteresis so we don't oscillate during short bursts. hysteresis helped a lot for microbursty traffic but increases time to adopt better kernels under sustained load.

raj: can you share the prewarm snippet? we might add it to our dedicated startup hooks.

anna: prewarm I used (quick script):
```bash
# run in container at startup
for seq in 512 1024 2048 4096; do
  python infra/bench/run_one_kernel.py --model llama2-70b-q8 --kernel flashattn-v3 --seq $seq --batch 1 || true
done
```

benchbot: summary: prewarm reduced observed p99 from ~210ms -> ~100ms in H100 flashv3 tests, median unchanged.

kevin: that aligns. other lever: routing policy. for bursty low-rps we prefer kernels with deterministic startup (flashv2 or vendor lib) even if median slightly higher. for steady high throughput (>10rps) flashv3 gives better median and throughput. we should encode this as a routing rule. :rocket:

raj: proposal for runtime policy (pseudo-JSON):
```json
{
  "kernel_policy": [
    {"when": {"recent_qps_avg": "<5", "burst_metric": true}, "prefer": "flashv2", "hysteresis_s": 120},
    {"when": {"recent_qps_avg": ">=5"}, "prefer": "flashv3", "hysteresis_s": 60}
  ]
}
```

sarah: i'd also add a fallback to vendor-lib on repeated compile failures or if p99 crosses threshold for >2m. fallback helps avoid prolonged regressions.

anna: good call. i'll spin a canary tomorrow: 5% traffic in eu-west-1 will use flashv3 w/ prewarm and the above policy. will report numbers. thanks for the quick ideas. :eyes:

raj: one more thought — can we capture the first-compile penalty in our cost model? it matters for short-lived functions. if we show engineers the tail penalty they might prefer q4f16 + flashv2 for low-latency interactive flows.

kevin: agreed. also add a metric for "first-request-latency" per worker after boot or after kernel update. we can expose it in console as "kernel_warmup_p99".

anna: noted. i'll create an eval run and share the tiny dashboard screenshots. thanks all. :thumbsup:
